references.scene: Register COMMON. A quiet landscape of mesmerizing beauty, not an action scene. A moonlit black-pine ravine opens towards a distant narrow ember reflection in a winding river. Foreground: intimate wet charcoal rocks, finely articulated moss-free roots, a curved leaning pine with every needle cluster and damp bark edge delicately catching silver light. Middle ground: overlapping ranks of pines with graduated mist and readable crowns. Far distance: the river disappears into folded dark mountains below sculpted low clouds and the slender crescent. Create a subtle circular embrace in the composition, like a place that shelters a secret. A tiny dark moth resting on the foreground bark is a discreet discoverable life detail, with refined silver-veined wings. The feeling is 'I want to return here'. Common rarity, extraordinary craftsmanship, breathtaking atmospheric depth, serene and restrained. This is the foundational landscape of the other three cards.
references.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Deliver ONE finished vertical 2:3 illustration for the shared collector-card universe LUNE inside Woop, ideally 1024x1536. This is bare FULL-ART artwork; the app adds its existing frame afterward. No card mockup, borders, medallions, captions, text, lettering, numerals, UI, watermark, or rarity symbols.
Art direction: an extraordinary, poetic world of deep night, cold neutral moonlight and restrained dark ember. Beautiful mysterious creatures and ancient wilderness, grounded material realism and exquisite cinematic matte painting, with the precision and emotional composition of a collector's fine-art plate. Quietly uncanny, solemn, intimate; no fairy-tale dragon, cute fantasy, armour, castles, magic runes, rainbow, neon, purple/cyan lighting, or game-poster clichés. An original universe, not Pokémon character designs.
All four rarity tiers have the SAME exceptional painting finish; rarity changes the staging and scale, never the craftsmanship. Preserve readable values: layered charcoal, pearl-grey moonlight, detailed shadow forms, ember-orange in small deliberate accents. Dark does NOT mean a black silhouette pasted into a black void. Softly sculpted clouds, light separating near/middle/far planes, tactile surfaces; no broad orange fog, no sunset wash, no floating glitter cloud. The ember feels like a distant surviving fire.
World continuity: a winding dark river, ancient black pines, stratified mist and a slender ember crescent appear across this universe. A single small crescent integrated naturally in the sky: asymmetrical sharp upper horn, slight hooked/barbed lower horn, warm ember contour, no icon tile. Visual hierarchy must read at thumbnail size and reward close inspection.
Composition: important subject anatomy and the moon stay within the central 76% width and below the top-left fifth where the existing frame's medallion will sit. Do NOT draw that frame. Edge areas remain richly painted environment. No cropped feet, antlers or wing tips when the subject is specified as fully visible.

references.scene: Register RARE. Three graceful black bats resting closely together on the underside of an ancient arched pine branch over the dark river valley. Anatomically convincing, delicate faces with a sober intelligent presence, finely groomed charcoal fur, warm dark eyes, elegant folded wings with nuanced translucent smoky membranes. One bat has quietly opened a wing partway towards the thin moonlight, producing a beautiful asymmetric fan shape and showing tiny material details; the other two nestle calmly. They are small mysterious inhabitants of a vast world, not cute mascot cartoons or snarling monsters. The trio is central and large enough to read at card size. The rough branch curves through the composition; rich sculpted clouds, distant pines, layered mist and the same thin ember river beyond them. Gentle silver light separates every head and wing from the environment, with a minute ember rim reflected from below. The slender hooked crescent hangs in the distant upper-right sky. Intimate, tender without being sugary, visually unforgettable and luxuriously finished.

references.scene: Register EPIC. An immense black bird of prey glides through a monumental opening in charcoal storm clouds above the same moonlit pine valley. A unique, memorable avian silhouette: powerful narrow head, long elegantly splayed primary feathers, black ash-soft layered plumage touched by fine ember traces only along a few feather edges. It is a living bird, NOT a bird made of fire, not a phoenix illustration cliché. Its entire wing span fits inside the safe central width, seen in an astonishing three-quarter angle with one wing lifted towards the foreground and the other carving into distant cloud depth, visually immense while anatomically coherent. Below, the river's tiny copper thread and miniature forests establish staggering scale. Clouds form sculptural masses with pearl moonlit faces and deep shadow valleys; restrained dark ember lives inside a few far cloud bellies. The little barbed crescent remains present in an opening away from the head. The image feels like a rare witnessed event, awe-inspiring, silent, poetic; composition as strong as a museum painting. Feather-by-feather structure and exceptional layered light, controlled palette.

references.scene: Register LEGENDARY, the unquestionable masterpiece of the set. An extraordinary black stag stands on a narrow wet obsidian shelf in the heart of the ancient river valley at night. Complete creature visible, elegant believable anatomy and long slender legs, a grave luminous gaze, no snarling. Its coat is living black velvet with precise obsidian-like lustrous highlights, not a metal robot. Magnificent tall asymmetrical branching antlers with a memorable sculptural silhouette rise within the safe framing; fine dark ember glows only at a few tips like the last warmth in charcoal, never flames or magical neon branches. Heroic low but intimate viewpoint, body turned three-quarter and head quietly facing us: a personal encounter. Foreground polished dark rock and a fine sheet of flowing water reflect the antlers in a broken narrow ember trace. Middle ground monumental black pine ridges stepping down into five distinct mist layers; distant river, impossible depth, clouds sculpted like geological strata. A perfectly placed restrained crescent beyond the antlers gives a quiet visual echo, not a halo. Moonlight choreographed over shoulder, eye, chest, water and distant clouds; every plane painted with obsessive tactile detail. A breath-stopping dark poetic creature with sovereign presence. Legendary through astonishing composition, depth and materials, never ornamental clutter or fairy-tale spectacle. An artwork you would treasure.
